A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references and supplements. The original experimental appendix can be matched from Appendix C in v1 to Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, accuracy and runtime experiments on 11 real structure-from-motion scenes, and supplementary sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds spectral-baseline results in Table D.1 and per-scene matrix-indefiniteness statistics in Table 1.

M1.justification: The proposed SDP-CSO(3) algorithm retains its Hessian-derived weights, linear objective, convex-hull constraints and solution procedure. The new spectral construction is evaluated as an additional baseline.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic rotation-averaging scenarios and 11 real structure-from-motion scenes. The spectral comparison and matrix diagnostics use existing coverage; the supplementary experiments are retained under renumbered Appendix D.

E2.justification: Table D.1 adds an anisotropic spectral baseline associated with Arie-Nachimson et al., alongside the retained SDP-O(3)-ISO and SDP-CSO(3) methods. The comparator sets in the main experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Synthetic noise distributions, camera counts, missing-edge settings, real-data preprocessing, gauge alignment, error metrics and solver tolerances are retained. The added spectral results use the existing real-data evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a diagnostic analysis measuring the proportion of indefinite cost matrices in each scene, supporting the mechanism discussed in Section 4.1. Existing parameterization, noisy-edge and graph-density analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 synthetic instances per configuration and 1000 instances for the rank experiment, with the same histogram, scatter and median reporting. No new seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table D.1 adds spectral results for all 11 scenes. For example, Temple Singapore has spectral Mahalanobis/angular errors of 0.719/0.46 degrees versus SDP-CSO(3)'s 1.076/0.55 degrees. Table 1 adds indefinite-matrix rates of 77–100%. All 33 original main-table rows are unchanged; retained supplemental scores differ only by rounding.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the sign in the squared cross-product identity preceding Equation (5). New Appendix C derives a spectral relation under noise-free assumptions, and Appendix A removes an inverse-covariance equality from Equation (A.1). The principal theorem, corollary and SDP derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim certifiably optimal anisotropic rotation averaging, explain the failure of determinant-ignoring relaxations, and propose the stronger convex-hull relaxation. Claims of empirical tightness and generally improved reconstruction accuracy retain the same scope.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds an explicit discussion of the existing point-estimate and unimodal Gaussian assumptions, explaining the limitation posed by multiple modes from perceptual aliasing and identifying alternative treatments. Existing cautions about ground truth, noise realizations and computational expense remain.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from a project webpage to a direct GitHub repository pointer. Appendix C documents the added spectral baseline's matrix construction and solution extraction. Core solver settings and data-processing instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Adds Arie-Nachimson et al. for the spectral baseline and Birdal et al., Lerman and Shi, Shi et al., and Zach et al. for multimodal or cycle-consistency alternatives. The central positioning against isotropic and Cayley-map approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits refine the abstract, Section 4.1 and conclusion, standardize relative-rotation subscripts, and add a funding acknowledgment. Inserting the spectral appendix renumbers the existing experimental appendix from C to D; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands dataset annotations and its caption to include indefinite-matrix percentages. Supplemental Table C.1 becomes D.1 with spectral rows and reduced numerical precision. Existing graphical content is preserved, with several figures relocated.

improvement.justification: The matrix-indefiniteness diagnostics strengthen the empirical support for the failure mechanism, the multimodal-noise discussion clarifies applicability, and the sign correction improves mathematical accuracy. These are limited gains around a stable core contribution. The added spectral comparison broadens the evidence, but Appendix C derives D^-1 N R = R and then specifies extraction using N-I without explaining the normalization, limiting the clarity and reproducibility of that addition.
